{{short description|American mathematical statistician (1931–2022)}}
'''James Pickands III''' (September 4, 1931 – March 9, 2022) was an American mathematical statistician known for his contribution to [[extreme value theory]] and [[Stochastic process|stochastic processes]].<ref name=ims>{{Cite web |title=Institute of Mathematical Statistics {{!}} Obituary: James Pickands III 1931–2022 |url=https://imstat.org/2022/12/13/obituary-james-pickands-iii-1931-2022/ |access-date=2023-02-23 |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=James Pickands III, Wharton |url=https://almanac.upenn.edu/articles/james-pickands-iii-wharton |access-date=2023-02-23 |website=almanac.upenn.edu |language=en}}</ref>

Pickands was born in [[Euclid, Ohio]] to James Pickands II and Sarah Cornelia Martin.<ref>{{Cite web |title=James Pickands II |url=https://ancestors.familysearch.org/en/9Q2S-2K3/james-pickands-ii-1906-1978 |access-date=2023-04-02 |website=ancestors.familysearch.org}}</ref><ref name=wharton></ref> He studied at [[Yale University]], where he obtained his bachelor's degree. He then moved to [[Columbia University]], where he received his PhD under Simeon Berman in 1965. While at Columbia, Pickands also worked with [[Emil Gumbel]],<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Gumbel |first1=E. J. |last2=Iii |first2=James Pickands |date=1967 |title=Probability Tables for the Extremal Quotient |url=https://projecteuclid.org/journals/annals-of-mathematical-statistics/volume-38/issue-5/Probability-Tables-for-the-Extremal-Quotient/10.1214/aoms/1177698708.full |journal=The Annals of Mathematical Statistics |volume=38 |issue=5 |pages=1541–1551 |doi=10.1214/aoms/1177698708 |issn=0003-4851|doi-access=free }}</ref> and developed interests in [[extreme value theory]].

Pickands served in the US Army in [[Aberdeen, Maryland]]<ref name=wharton>{{Cite web |last=Yuen |first=Gloria |date=2022-05-06 |title=James Pickands III |url=https://news.wharton.upenn.edu/in-memoriam/2022/05/james-pickands-iii/ |access-date=2023-02-23 |website=News |language=en-US}}</ref> after graduating from Columbia university. He briefly taught at [[Virginia Tech]] as an assistant professor before joining the [[Wharton School of the University of Pennsylvania|Wharton School]] at the [[University of Pennsylvania]] in 1969 as an associate professor, where he stayed for the rest of his career.<ref name=ims></ref>

Pickands had three doctoral students, including [[Bruce Cooil]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=James Pickands, III - The Mathematics Genealogy Project |url=https://www.genealogy.math.ndsu.nodak.edu/id.php?id=93833 |access-date=2023-12-10 |website=www.genealogy.math.ndsu.nodak.edu}}</ref>

== Personal life ==
Pickands's great-grandfather James S. Pickands (1839–1896)<ref>{{Cite web |date=2018-06-18 |title=PICKANDS, JAMES S. |url=https://case.edu/ech/articles/p/pickands-james-s |access-date=2023-04-02 |website=Encyclopedia of Cleveland History {{!}} Case Western Reserve University |language=en}}</ref> is a cofounder of the American shipping company [[Pickands Mather Group]].
